title: Workflow document
description: The Agent-authored Workflow. A node is either a STAGE (a leaf that holds calls and its frozen checklists) or a WORKFLOW (a composite that holds children and reads their verdicts). 'Tree' describes only the shape this structure may take; the semantics are 'a Workflow contains Workflows'. ORDER comes only from depends_on: the order nodes are written in carries no meaning, and two nodes with no dependency between them are unordered -- the Agent, which executes every call itself, may run them in any order or at the same time. This document is judged, not scheduled: nothing here runs anything.

guidance.description: Provenance only. Which guidance document the author followed.

status.description: Lifecycle state of this revision. Every value here is one the engine can emit or act on: guide.py refuses to reopen a terminal revision (completed, failed, invalid, superseded), and aggregation.py produces running, suspended, and completed for TaskResult.workflow_status. It defaults to draft.

nodeId.description: Unique among SIBLINGS only. The character class excludes '/' and whitespace: a path is built by joining ids with '/', so an id containing '/' would produce a path that walk() emits and resolve() cannot reach. '.' is allowed -- nothing parses it out of a path.

dependencyRef.description: A reference to a node, walked FROM the declaring node: '..' moves to its parent, any other segment names a child of where the walk has arrived. So '../mass' is a sibling, '../../site/street-trees' reaches into another branch, and '..' alone is the parent. It is relative, not absolute, because a reusable subtree does not know where it will be placed and so could not name its own siblings otherwise. A bare 'mass' resolves to the declaring node's own CHILD -- a node it already waits for -- and is refused with the spelling that was meant.

node.description: Discriminated by 'kind'. Exactly one branch matches, because the branches close their own properties.

required.description: Defaults to true when absent. A required node must complete for its parent to complete; an optional one may be omitted, and omitting it never fails the parent.

depends_on.description: Nodes that must complete before this stage runs, each written from this node. A dependency MAY cross branches -- '../../site/street-trees' declared under '/buildings/...' is legal, and is why this is a walked reference and not a sibling id. An ancestor's dependency already gates this stage, so repeat it here only when the ordering is genuinely local. This is the ONLY source of order: written order means nothing, and two nodes with no dependency between them may run in any order or at the same time. A cycle is refused, including one formed with the implicit rule that a composite waits for its own children.

Nodes that must complete before this composite runs, each written from this node. See the stage branch: a dependency may cross branches, a cycle is refused, and this is the only source of order. A composite's dependency gates its WHOLE subtree -- no descendant may run until it is satisfied -- so a leaf does NOT repeat its ancestors' references. Declare the ordering once, at the level where it is true.

acceptance_checklist.description: Checks that read DESCENDANT verdicts. A composite never reads its own.

stage_kind.description: Which lifecycle this leaf follows, which decides what must be frozen before its first side effect. A change freezes execution and acceptance; an investigation freezes scope and stop conditions; a planning stage proves goals, constraints, call feasibility, dependencies and risks. Defaults to 'change' when absent.

calls.description: An EMPTY list is legal, and is how a leaf that runs no host call is written -- a human review, or a checkpoint whose evidence someone submits. A required STAGE must declare at least one call, which the validator enforces; a leaf marked required:false need not. Remember that 'calls' itself is still required: omit the key and the document is not a stage.

call_id.description: Unique inside its STAGE, which is the scope every other reference to it lives in. Plain by convention: an id is addressed by itself, never by a prefix.

target.description: The MCP server and tool. Optional in a guidance document, where a call names a role and the caller binds the target after confirming the live server.

depends_on.description: Call ids inside the same STAGE that must complete first.

evidence_required.description: Defaults to true. An item reporting pass or warn while naming no evidence is downgraded to unknown -- a claim with nothing behind it is not proof. The evidence is supplied when the RESULT is submitted, not here: the result document carries 'evidence_refs', a non-empty list of strings naming what was looked at. An item derived from a call gets its reference from the engine, so this bites hardest on an item with an empty call_ids.

call_ids.description: Satisfied when every named call succeeded. A call with no reported result counts as failed. An EMPTY list is legal and means the item derives from no call: it is satisfied only by an explicit result the Agent submits, which is how a human judgement enters the record.

operator.description: The comparison vocabulary. What each one compares, given the value read at 'actual_path': manual -- nothing; it awaits a human verdict. tool_succeeded -- the call's own status; no actual_path needed. exists -- the value is not null. truthy -- the value is truthy. equals -- the value equals 'expected'. set_equals -- the value's SET equals 'expected's set, so order and duplicates do not matter, and set_equals with an empty list asserts the value is empty. count_equals -- len(value) equals 'expected', so a LIST or OBJECT is counted by its item or key count. within_tolerance -- the value is numerically within 'tolerance' of 'expected'; the comparison is symmetric. A comparison needing logic of its own belongs in a call that returns a boolean, not in a new operator.

verdict.description: One node's verdict, and the ONLY thing a composite check observes when it reads a descendant. It is not the task vocabulary: a NODE is 'pass' or 'fail', a TASK is 'succeeded' or 'failed'. Two independent authors given this schema without this line guessed 'succeeded' and 'pass' for the same field; the first produces a check that can never pass.

source_call_id.description: A call declared in this same STAGE, or null. A STAGE check may not read a node. Required for every operator except 'manual', which reads nothing; the VALIDATOR enforces that split, not this schema, so do not read the absence of a required array as permission.

actual_path.description: Where in the call's evidence to read, as a path of keys into the result -- object keys, or a digit for a list index. An EMPTY path reads the whole evidence view, which is an object that always carries status, target, preserved_relations, lost_relations, artifact_count, artifacts, warnings and errors before any of the call's own outputs. Do not leave it empty to mean 'the call's output': the view is larger than the output, so a count_equals over it counts those fixed fields too.

expected.description: What the check compares against: the value found in the call's own result at 'actual_path'. If the path is absent from the result the check is UNKNOWN, not failed, so a missing field is never silently read as a wrong value.

tolerance.description: Required when the operator is within_tolerance; the comparison is symmetric.

evidence_required.description: Defaults to true. A check reporting pass or warn while naming no evidence is downgraded to unknown. A check that reads a call gets its reference from the engine, so this field decides whether a MANUAL check can pass at all: submit its result with 'evidence_refs', a non-empty list of strings, or the check stays unknown however many times it is submitted.

operator.description: A composite observes exactly ONE descendant's verdict -- a single word -- so 'equals' against a verdict word is the only comparison that carries meaning, and 'manual' is the only one that observes nothing and awaits a human. Every other operator applied to a word yields an accident rather than a judgement: tool_succeeded and exists would always pass, count_equals and within_tolerance always fail.

source_call_id.description: Always null on a composite. A workflow check reads a DESCENDANT, never a call, so the field is pinned to null rather than merely unused: allowing a string here would let a document carry a call reference the engine can never honour.

source_node.description: A DESCENDANT of the declaring node, as a relative path. Must not begin with '/': an absolute-looking path would be resolved relatively and mean different nodes at different depths. Required for an 'equals' check; a 'manual' check reads no descendant and omits it.

expected.description: What the check compares against. A source_node check observes exactly ONE descendant's verdict, so this is a verdict word -- NOT a list of descendants, and NOT a task status such as 'succeeded'. A check reads one descendant: to assert several, declare one check each, or add a composite node whose verdict they roll up into. Two blind authors given this schema without this line wrote a list and wrote 'succeeded'; both produce checks that can never pass.

evidence_required.description: Defaults to true. A composite check reads a descendant's verdict, which the engine already has, so this field only decides whether a MANUAL composite check can pass: submit its result with 'evidence_refs', a non-empty list of strings.
